newsitem.title: USA: N.J. Turnpike says revenues, traffic surge in Q1.
newsitem.headline: N.J. Turnpike says revenues, traffic surge in Q1.

text.p: The New Jersey Turnpike Authority said revenue and traffic volume both exceeded expections in the first quarter, jumping 6.7 percent and 6.2 percent, respectively.
The agency's budget had projected just two percent increases in both figures for the period.
Passenger car traffic increased a record 6.6 percent for the first three months of the year compared to the same period last year, while commercial traffic rose 3.6 percent, the authority said.
Feeding off the higher traffic volume, revenue also surged during the quarter. Collections from passenger cars and commercial vehicles rose 8.4 percent and 4.1 percent, respectively.
Total revenues were expected to be $82.8 million, but collections actually came to $86.7 million. Toll revenue alone exceeded projections by 4.7 percent.

The authority attributed some of the growth to a mild winter, which prompted more drivers to hit the road. But it said even adjusted for weather, traffic jumped 3.4 percent and revenue rose 4.1 percent.
Operating expenses, meanwhile, declined $5.9 million for the first quarter, the authority said.

"What all these figures reflect is that we're doing things right," Authority Chairman Frank McDermott said in a statement announcing the results. "The authority is now being run as would any good business, with a sharp eye towards curtailing unnecessary expenditures and improving customer service."
